name: Treaty with the Sauk and Foxes, 1836 (cession of Keokuk's Reserve)
aka: Treaty of September 28, 1836, Sac and Fox
citation: 7 Stat. 517 (as printed in Kappler); the Indian Claims Commission cites it as 7 Stat. 520
nations: Meskwaki Nation (Sac & Fox Tribe of the Mississippi in Iowa)
Sac and Fox Nation of Missouri in Kansas and Nebraska
promises: Article 2: $30,000 in June 1837 and then $10,000 a year in specie for ten years, paid at the treaty ground opposite Rock Island or where the President named.
Article 2: $48,458.87 1/2 to pay debts found justly due from the Sac and Fox to individuals, any balance to go to the Sac and Fox; $1,000 to the widow and children of agent Felix St. Vrain.
Article 3: about two hundred horses, as many as $9,341 would buy, delivered at the June 1837 annuity payment.
Articles 4 and 5: sums for seven named children of Sac and Fox mothers and for the two children of John Connoly, at the Sac and Fox request.
In return the Sac and Fox ceded the reservation of four hundred sections set apart by Article 2 of the treaty of September 21, 1832 (Keokuk's Reserve on the Iowa River).
landTaken: The Indian Claims Commission found Royce Area 226 contained 400 sections, or 217,600 acres, in southeast Iowa, and that the Sac and Fox and the Iowa each owned an undivided one-half interest in it (20 Ind. Cl. Comm. 439, findings 4 and 46).
compensation: The Commission found the total consideration the United States agreed to pay the Sac and Fox under this treaty was $192,000.12, plus $1,056.00 paid to the Missouri Sac and Fox under the treaty of October 21, 1837. It found the Sac and Fox one-half interest worth $136,000.00 and held that the United States agreed to pay, and did pay, more than full value; the claim in Docket 209 was to be dismissed (finding 49, May 12, 1969).
today: The Indian Claims Commission found no evidence of undue pressure, coercion or deception in the making of this treaty (finding 46) and no unconscionable price for the Sac and Fox share. The Iowa Nation's half interest in the same tract was ceded by a different treaty, of October 19, 1838. On appeal the Court of Claims sent the valuations back for fuller reasons (196 Ct. Cl. 548, 1971); on remand the Commission again found the $193,056.12 paid exceeded the $136,000 value of the Sac and Fox half interest and dismissed Docket 209 (Final Award on Remand, November 23, 1973, 32 Ind. Cl. Comm. 256).

openQuestions: Statute citation differs: Kappler prints 7 Stat. 517; the Indian Claims Commission cites the treaty as 7 Stat. 520. Not checked against the Statutes at Large.

The Commission's 1969 findings give the effective date as both October 13, 1837 (findings 46 and 49) and October 28, 1837 (finding 47), while Kappler records a proclamation of February 27, 1837. Ratification date left out.

Whether the ten annuity payments and the horses were delivered in full was not researched beyond the Commission's finding that $175,444.17 was disbursed under Article 2 and $9,341 spent under Article 3.
No Sac and Fox Nation or Meskwaki Nation account of this treaty was found online.

2026-11-08 sweep: Court of Claims and ICC full text searched for sac and fox, Keokuk reserve, 1836 and Royce 226; the 1971 remand and 1973 final award on remand again dismissed the claim for this cession (Docket 209); added to today. Status unchanged.

plain.promised: The Sac and Fox sold Keokuk's Reserve, 400 sections on the Iowa River, for $30,000, ten yearly payments of $10,000, money to pay their debts and about two hundred horses.
plain.happened: No breach has been documented yet. The Indian Claims Commission found in 1969 that the United States paid more than full value for the Sac and Fox share and found no duress.
plain.today: The Sac and Fox claim for more payment for this land was dismissed by the Commission.
